data.one_liner: Cubits and widgets to eliminate boilerplate for single requests and paginated pages.
data.what_it_does: Provides specialized cubits like RequestCubit and PaginatedCubit alongside accompanying UI builders to handle loading, refreshing, error, and empty states for API requests and infinite scrolling lists.
use_when: Building pages that perform single HTTP or CQRS requests with loading, error, and success states.
Implementing paginated lists with infinite scrolling and automatic next-page fetching.
Eliminating repetitive state management boilerplate around Bloc/Cubit async calls.
avoid_when: Not using the flutter_bloc ecosystem or state management architecture.
Building simple local UI state that doesn't involve asynchronous network requests.
strengths: Reduces boilerplate for standard request-response and pagination flows.
Built-in request deduplication, caching, and refresh support.
Global configuration provider for default loaders, error widgets, and request modes.
weaknesses: Tied strictly to the bloc/cubit state management pattern.
Requires writing custom subclasses and mappers for each request type.

alternatives.name: bloc
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want raw state management without opinions on request and pagination abstractions.

alternatives.name: flutter_bloc
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides foundational state management primitives without specific request/pagination cubit wrappers.

data.minimal_example:
RequestCubitBuilder(
  cubit: context.read<ProjectDetailsCubit>(),
  onLoading: (context) => const Center(child: CircularProgressIndicator()),
  onSuccess: (context, data) => ListView(children: [Text(data.id)]),
)
